The events of the row that stands now, without those of an earlier one

log_current_life.Rd

A record id can be used twice: deleted, and made again by somebody else for another request. The log keeps both lives under the same record, and everything below the newest creation belongs to a row that no longer exists. The creation itself is the first event of the row that stands now, and stays: a row with one life is answered whole, as before the cut.

Usage

log_current_life(events)

Arguments

events

The events of one record, newest first.

Value

The events from the newest creation on, or all of them when there is none.

Details

Which event is newest comes from the order of the answer, REDCap's own, newest first, as for log_creators(), which names as the creator the author of this same event; the stamps are to the minute, and two lives can share one. The creation is read as log_creators() reads it, from the start of action, whose wording was measured on 2026-09-02. Read as a guard, a wording that does not match cuts nothing, and the log is read whole as before; log_creators() then names nobody, and the round holds the row.

Only the creation cuts, and not the deletion, whose wording was never measured. Nothing is lost by it, since the deletion of an earlier life stands below the creation of the current one. And an event that only reads like a deletion, inside the current life, would cut that life's own changes in the direction that grants: below it may stand a change by somebody else, which the round would then carry out with nobody asked.

Read by log_of_record(), so by every reader of a row's log.
